title: CF Meet Numbering common v1
description: The canonical vocabulary and messages of services/numbering (Part IV Workstreams C-D, ADR 0033): Number Resource identity (CF Meet ids are canonical; provider identifiers never appear), type, capabilities with provenance, opaque provider binding references, inventory observations, reservations, DCN assignments with ownership and routing references, routing profiles, lifecycle transitions, the trusted context and the error envelope. Values equal the database CHECK constraints and the Rust domain types (a conformance test compares them). Full public number search / provisioning APIs are later workstreams.

Revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency revision: 1 at creation, +1 on every effective change. Writers state the revision they expect; a stale one is VERSION_CONFLICT.

NumberResourceId.description: The canonical CF Meet identity of a public number (Number Resource). Independent of any provider identifier; never changes across provider replacement or porting.

E164.description: A normalized E.164 number. Exposed only by the internal Number Resource view to authorized services; never in events, logs or errors.

CountryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country stated by the inventory source (never inferred).

LifecycleState.description: The canonical Number Resource lifecycle (Part IV D2). Transitions follow one centralized policy (database function number_lifecycle_allowed). UNKNOWN_PROVIDER_STATE is left only by reconciliation with evidence; irreversible provider actions are never repeated while a resource is in it.

InventorySource.description: Origin of a resource. SYNTHETIC_TEST is test inventory, never a real public number, usable only by SANDBOX / TEST environments; PRODUCTION never uses it.

NumberType.description: Classification, set only from evidence (never inferred from the E.164 format or from SMS support).

Capability.description: Canonical capability types (Part IV D4). Voice / SMS / MMS are routable (served by a provider binding); the others are number-class attributes.

CapabilityStatus.description: VERIFIED only with evidence (never for synthetic inventory); RESTRICTED / WITHDRAWN / EXPIRED / REVOKED do not grant the capability. REVOKED is re-enabled only by an operator or reconciliation.

ReservationStatus.description: PENDING until a provider hold is confirmed (HELD); UNKNOWN when the hold outcome is uncertain. EXPIRED / CANCELLED / CONVERTED / FAILED are final.

ReleaseState.description: Whether a provider hold was given back. An expired or cancelled reservation does NOT imply a provider release: a held live number stays RESERVED with PENDING release until evidence.

AssignmentStatus.description: DCN assignment states (Part IV D6). ACTIVE is reachable only from ACTIVATING (and back from SUSPENDED) and only once every routed family is READY; one open (not CLOSED) assignment per number. ACTIVE -> CLOSED only by an internal transfer to a successor of the same legal owner (close reason TRANSFERRED_INTERNALLY).

OwnerKind.description: PRINCIPAL for PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL numbers; ORGANIZATION for every organizational class.

OwnershipClass.description: Provider-independent ownership classes (Part IV D7). An organization-owned number routed to an employee (EMPLOYEE_DIRECT) remains organizational property.

VoiceTargetKind.description: Voice routing target: opaque CF Meet ids of Calling / enterprise constructs (principal, professional identity, endpoint, extension, ring group, queue, IVR, department, shared team, voicemail, approved forwarding), never SIP or provider data. The kinds a number may use are bounded by its ownership class (TARGET_NOT_PERMITTED).

SmsTargetKind.description: SMS routing target (opaque CF Meet ids): a principal, an application, a shared-team or department inbox; bounded by the ownership class.

EnvironmentKind.description: The customer application environment (from Platform Access).

CostEvidence.description: Whether a cost is known from a source.

UncertainOperation.description: The external operation whose outcome is unknown (UNKNOWN_PROVIDER_STATE).

ReasonCode.description: Stable UPPER_SNAKE_CASE reason of a change.

CapabilityFact.description: The current record of one capability, with provenance and effective date (history is kept by Numbering).

ProviderBindingRef.description: The provider-independent view of a provider binding: an opaque binding reference. The provider identifier and the provider's own reference never leave Numbering.

NumberResource.description: GET /internal/v1/number-resources/{id} (permission number-resource.read): the canonical Number Resource for Calling / Telephony.

InventoryObservation.description: One inventory observation as Numbering records it (append-only). An observation is evidence that a number was offered; it is never an allocation. The internal provider key is not part of the contract.

Reservation.description: A reservation of the caller's trusted scope (other scopes: NOT_FOUND). PENDING until the provider hold is confirmed (HELD). Ending it never assumes a provider release: providerReleaseState stays PENDING / UNKNOWN until the provider's release is evidenced.

Ownership.description: The owner of a DCN assignment; immutable on the record (a new owner is a new assignment).

RoutingRef.description: The pinned routing profile revision of an assignment.

DcnAssignment.description: A DCN assignment of the caller's trusted scope: the legal owner (immutable on the record), the pinned routing revision and the transfer links (an internal transfer closes the predecessor and opens a successor of the same owner).

DcnAssignmentList.description: GET /v1/numbers/assignments: the caller scope's assignments, newest first (keyset pages, optional status / ownershipClass filters).

AssignmentHistoryEntry.description: One append-only history row of an assignment.

RoutingTarget.description: A routing target: a kind and, unless NONE, an opaque CF Meet reference.

RoutingProfile.description: One revision of a versioned routing profile (opaque ids; exactly one CURRENT revision per profile; superseded revisions are kept).

LifecycleTransition.description: One recorded Number Resource lifecycle transition (append-only audit).

TrustedContext.description: The trusted context of a customer request, taken ONLY from the authority chain Platform Access returns for the presented credential (cfmeet.platform-access.identity AuthorityChain). A tenant, application or environment id in a request never becomes authority; a SAFETY_ONLY authority is refused (Numbering has no safety operation).

InventoryClass.description: Which catalog governs a number: synthetic test inventory has its own catalog, never the real one.

CatalogSource.description: Where a catalog fact comes from. SYNTHETIC_TEST is test data, never real.

CatalogVerification.description: VERIFIED only with evidence; SYNTHETIC exactly for the synthetic catalog. Real numbers need VERIFIED catalog facts.

CapabilityChangeKind.description: How a capability record changed the effective truth.

CapabilityReason.description: Why a capability is not supported / not usable (fail closed).

ExternalVerificationNotice.description: The fixed wording on every voice / SMS capability. CF Meet never guarantees acceptance by WhatsApp, banks, social platforms or any OTP / third-party verification service.
ExternalVerificationNotice.const: Supports voice and SMS where provisioned; third-party verification compatibility varies by service and number type.

Limitations.description: Closed limitation vocabulary. externalVerification is never a guarantee.

CountryCatalogEntry.description: The CURRENT country entry of an inventory class.

NumberTypeCatalogEntry.description: A CURRENT number-type entry (generic: provider applicability is internal). Capabilities in neither list are unknown and treated as unsupported.

CatalogCountryView.description: GET /v1/numbers/catalog/countries/{countryCode}: the catalog of the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: synthetic; PRODUCTION: real).

CapabilityProvenance.description: Where a resolved capability's truth comes from. carrierConfirmed is never true for synthetic inventory.

EffectiveCapability.description: One resolved capability: supported (catalog AND this number's valid evidence) and usable now (supported; routable ones also need an ACTIVE number with an active binding serving them).

CapabilityResolution.description: GET /internal/v1/number-resources/{id}/capabilities and GET /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/capabilities: every canonical capability resolved from one consistent snapshot, with the revisions consumers compare to reject stale decisions.

PublishNumberTypeRequest.description: POST /v1/admin/catalog/number-types (numbers.admin, X-CF-Operator). Number-class attributes follow the type.

CatalogWithdrawal.description: The catalog revision that withdrew an entry.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error codes. PRECONDITION_FAILED / CONFLICT carry the domain rule in `reason`.

Error.description: The error envelope (Cache-Control: no-store). Never contains a number, provider reference, credential or database text.

KycStatus.description: The KYC case lifecycle: DRAFT → EVIDENCE_REQUIRED → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED, with MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED, REJECTED, EXPIRED and REVOKED (the same edge set in Rust and SQL; APPROVED → APPROVED is a revalidation renewal).

RequirementType.description: What a KYC requirement asks the subject to prove.

EvidenceContentType.description: Accepted evidence content (minimum data; magic bytes must match).

SubjectKind.description: Who is verified: an individual for PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL numbers, an organization for organizational ones.

RequirementScope.description: BASE: the requirements of a selector; PROVIDER_EXTENSION: added by the serving provider (merged, never replacing BASE).

TenantClassification.description: The tenant's trust classification (from Platform Access).

VerifierKind.description: Who verified: the deterministic test adapter (never in staging / production), the audited manual reviewer, or the system (lifecycle steps).

KycDecisionKind.description: Kinds of immutable KYC decision records.

AppealStatus.description: An appeal is resolved by the next final manual decision.

EligibilityOutcome.description: Eligibility outcomes. Precedence: DENIED > UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY > RISK_RESTRICTED > LIMIT_EXCEEDED > ADDITIONAL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED > KYC_REQUIRED > PENDING_REVIEW > ELIGIBLE.

EligibilityReasonCode.description: Why an eligibility outcome applies (fail closed: unknown is a refusal).

KycRequirements.description: GET /v1/numbers/kyc/requirements/{countryCode}/{numberType}/{ownershipClass}: the requirements in force for the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: explicitly non-production policies). Unknown mandatory requirements are KYC_REQUIREMENTS_UNKNOWN (422), never an empty list.

RequirementSet.description: A published requirement set version (administration view).

PublishRequirementsRequest.description: POST /v1/admin/kyc/requirements (numbers.admin, X-CF-Operator): a new version of a selector's requirement set (supersedes the current one). REAL requirements need a non-synthetic source; SYNTHETIC ones are SYNTHETIC_TEST only.

CreateKycCaseRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases (numbers.kyc.manage, optional Idempotency-Key). subjectRef is an opaque CF Meet reference (a principal or organization id) — never personal data.

KycEvidence.description: Evidence METADATA (content is never returned outside the privileged access route; no object key, digest or key id).

KycCase.description: A KYC case of the caller's scope (other scopes' cases are NOT_FOUND). Carries ids, statuses and reason codes only.

requirements.description: The exact requirement snapshot the case was opened against.

SubmitEvidenceRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/evidence (numbers.kyc.manage). Content is sealed (AES-256-GCM, bound to the evidence id) and stored privately; ≤ 5 MiB decoded. The kind must be accepted by a requirement of the case.

SubmitKycCaseRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/submit: every mandatory requirement needs accepted ACTIVE evidence (else MANDATORY_EVIDENCE_MISSING).

KycDecision.description: One immutable KYC decision record (one per case revision).

KycAppeal.description: An appeal of a REJECTED / REVOKED case (back to UNDER_REVIEW for a human reviewer).

KycCaseHistory.description: GET /v1/numbers/kyc/cases/{caseId}/history: the immutable decision history and appeals.

ReviewKycCaseRequest.description: POST /v1/admin/kyc/cases/{caseId}/decisions (numbers.admin, X-CF-Operator): an explicit, reason-coded decision on a case UNDER_REVIEW naming the ACTIVE evidence examined. APPROVE never bypasses a mandatory requirement; validForDays may shorten, never extend, the policy validity.

KycReviewResult.description: The case after a manual decision and the decision record.

AdminKycCase.description: GET /v1/admin/kyc/cases/{caseId}: the case with its scope, reviewer, evidence metadata, decisions, appeals and verification attempts.

requirements.description: The exact requirement snapshot the case was opened against.

EvidenceAccessRequest.description: POST /v1/admin/kyc/evidence/{evidenceId}/access (numbers.admin, X-CF-Operator): every read, denial and purged read is audited.

EvidenceContent.description: The privileged, audited evidence read (Cache-Control: no-store; integrity verified).

EligibilityRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/eligibility (numbers.kyc.read): may this scope request such a number? Evaluation only — never reserves or provisions.

EligibilityDecision.description: A recorded (append-only) eligibility decision with every reason. ELIGIBLE has no reasons and is valid until the earlier of its TTL and the KYC approval expiry; an assignment becomes ELIGIBLE only with such a decision of its own scope.

AssignmentKycStatus.description: GET /internal/v1/assignments/{assignmentId}/kyc-status (number-resource.read): whether the KYC basis of an assignment is in force (no evidence, no subject data).

ProviderCommandStatus.description: Durable provider command status. UNKNOWN (the request may have been acted on) leaves only through read-back reconciliation; it is never re-sent blindly.

ProviderCommandOperation.description: Provider-affecting operations executed as durable commands (RELEASE_HOLD: a reservation's provider hold given back on cancellation / expiry, Workstream H).

ProviderEventDisposition.description: What Numbering did with an authenticated provider event. RECONCILE_REQUESTED: an uncertain command is re-checked by read-back (an event never finalizes a command by itself); STALE: older than the newest version already applied; IGNORED_TERMINAL: never resurrects a released number; CONFLICT: drift, fail closed with an incident.

ProviderCallbackAck.description: POST /provider-callbacks/v1/{providerId}: the authenticated callback was stored once (or recognized as a redelivery). Never carries provider data.

HoldBasis.description: Why a reservation holds a number: a domain-level hold (D primitives), a recorded ELIGIBLE decision of the reserving scope, or a temporary hold before eligibility where policy permits it (never PRODUCTION; provisioning always requires eligibility).

ReservationConversion.description: What a CONVERTED reservation became: taken over by a DCN assignment, or a provisioned acquisition (Workstream I).

CreateReservationRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/reservations (Idempotency-Key required). The scope is the caller's trusted one; a body never names a tenant, application or environment.

capabilities.description: Routable capabilities the number is reserved for; each must be supported (E resolver).

ReservationList.description: GET /v1/numbers/reservations: the caller's reservations, newest first (keyset pages).

CountryList.description: GET /v1/numbers/countries: the supported countries of the caller's inventory class (SANDBOX / TEST: synthetic; PRODUCTION: real, verified).

NumberTypeList.description: GET /v1/numbers/countries/{countryCode}/number-types: the generic number-type entries in force, with their capability metadata.

SearchAvailability.description: AVAILABLE: offered by a fresh observation (reservable, never guaranteed); STALE: the newest observation expired (not reservable until observed again).

InventoryRefresh.description: How the inventory behind a search page was obtained: REFRESHED (a provider was asked now), CACHED (asked within the refresh interval), PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (a provider could not be reached; cached observations only), NOT_CONFIGURED (no provider serves the class, or live telecom is not allowed), NOT_REQUESTED (a later page).

KycIndicator.description: What the KYC requirements in force say about a search result (Workstream F): UNKNOWN when none are published (eligibility then fails closed).

NumberSearchResult.description: One search result: an OBSERVATION of a canonical Number Resource, never a reservation or a guarantee. Provider identifiers never appear.

items.description: A supported capability with its provenance (synthetic for test inventory; carrierConfirmed only for a verified real provider confirmation).

cost.description: Commercial facts as observed (an estimate until billing evidence exists).

observation.description: Freshness of the observation behind the result.

NumberSearchPage.description: GET /v1/numbers/search: one bounded page of the caller's inventory class (a country is required; keyset cursor bound to the query).

inventory.description: How the inventory behind the page was obtained.

AcquisitionStatus.description: PROVISIONING until the provider's acquisition is proven (PROVISIONED, with a binding), FAILED on a definite refusal (retryable), UNKNOWN while the outcome is reconciled from read-back (never resent).

RouteFamily.description: A capability family routed by one provider configuration: VOICE (carried by Telephony) or SMS (carried by the SMS Gateway).

RouteStatus.description: Provider route configuration: REQUESTED, CONFIGURED (provider acknowledgement evidence), FAILED, UNKNOWN (reconciled from read-back), SUPERSEDED.

RouteReadinessReason.description: Why a family is not ready to carry traffic.

FamilyReadiness.description: One family of a number: the provider route configured on the CURRENT binding AND acknowledged by the family's consumer.

Acquisition.description: A reservation being (or having been) provisioned for the caller's scope. PROVISIONED means the platform acquired the number — NOT an active customer number (that needs an eligible owner, routing and readiness: a DCN assignment). Provider identifiers and route references never appear.

liveRouting.description: false for synthetic test inventory: never live public routing.

AcquisitionList.description: GET /v1/numbers/acquisitions: the caller's acquisitions, newest first.

CreateAcquisitionRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/acquisitions (Idempotency-Key required): provision a reservation that holds the number.

ConfigureRoutesRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/acquisitions/{acquisitionId}/routes (Idempotency-Key required): configure the provider routes of these capabilities' families on the current binding.

NumberRoutes.description: GET /internal/v1/number-resources/{id}/routes: the current provider route configuration of every family and consumer readiness (internal; route references are opaque CF Meet ids).

RouteReadinessRequest.description: POST /internal/v1/number-resources/{id}/route-readiness (number-route.acknowledge): the consumer of the family (Telephony: VOICE, SMS Gateway: SMS) acknowledges the CONFIGURED revision it routes.

RoutingTargets.description: Where a number routes: one voice and one SMS target (kind NONE: not routed). Validated against the ownership class: a personal / professional number routes to its owner only; an employee's direct line to one employee; organizational classes to their constructs.

CreateAssignmentRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments (Idempotency-Key required): assign a PROVISIONED acquisition (acquisitionId) or a HELD reservation (reservationId) of the caller to its legal owner. Organizational classes belong to the authenticated organization and name no owner; PERSONAL / PROFESSIONAL name an owning principal Platform Access resolves ACTIVE in the caller's environment.

AssignmentRouting.description: GET /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/routing: the pinned routing revision, the number's routing revision (advanced by every routing change; routing grants are bound to it) and per-family readiness.

UpdateRoutingRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/routing: a new routing revision (same class, same owner). expectedRoutingRevision is the profile revision the caller saw (VERSION_CONFLICT otherwise).

OffboardingRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/offboarding: an EMPLOYEE_DIRECT number leaves the departing employee — unrouted (no replacement) or routed to a replacement (never the departing employee). The number stays the organization's.

TransferAssignmentRequest.description: POST /v1/numbers/assignments/{id}/transfer (Idempotency-Key required): within the same legal owner only. Same class: a routing revision. Another class of the same owner: the ACTIVE assignment closes (TRANSFERRED_INTERNALLY) and a successor opens, admitted on a re-evaluated eligibility decision of the new class and activated in the same transaction. A different owner is CROSS_OWNER_TRANSFER_UNSUPPORTED.

TransferResult.description: The outcome of an internal transfer.

PoolMember.description: A current member of an organizational pool.

usage.description: ASSIGNED while routed to a target, AVAILABLE while unrouted.

NumberPool.description: An organizational number pool of the caller's scope (organization-owned numbers only; an assignment is in at most one pool; usage / subscription policies are opaque references).

PoolMembership.description: A pool membership (ended memberships are kept as history).

AdminAssignmentHistoryEntry.description: One history row of any owner's assignment of a number (operator view).

AssignmentHistoryList.description: GET /v1/admin/number-resources/{id}/assignment-history: every owner's assignment history of a number, oldest first (numbers.admin, operator-attributed).
